findings.title: The missing-page rule is a suite-level test, but tasks 1.1-1.2 and design D2 put it in the file-local helper

walk_entry.title: The coverage check does not say what happens when docs/cli.md or docs/commands.md is absent

findings.recommendation: The walk added to the spec that the suite fails when an owing page is neither listed nor present, and that this runs over the suite's document set because 'a file-local check never sees an absent file'. Task 1.1 puts that rule inside commandCoverageFailures(surfaces, paths, workflowIds), and task 1.2 wires that helper into fileLocalFailures — a per-file check that receives neither the pending list nor the set of absent files, so built as written the rule can never fire, and task 1.3's scenario test for 'A missing owing page fails' has nothing to call. Design D2 says the same in one paragraph that first calls it 'a suite-level test alongside the per-file one' and then continues 'That makes it a member of the file-local set', where 'That' now reads as the suite-level test. Move the rule out of the helper: task 1.1 keeps the per-page match; add the suite-level assertion (the pending list plus allDocSurfaces, failing on an owing page in neither) as its own test in task 1.3 or the pending-rewrite suite, and reorder D2 so the file-local sentence follows the per-page check it describes.

commentary: Graded each resolved entry over its file, its applied ripples and its sweep scope; the residual check from the external pass's commit lists six files, all inside the edit records. F1's claims were re-read against source: the help string sits at program.ts:475 and command-registry.ts:190, registry parity's header says description is not compared, and init.ts refuses a profile outside core|custom. E4's Case 1 parses clean (rules_total 1, rules_open empty). The one regression is the cost of adding a whole-suite clause to a check whose every other rule is per-file: the spec carried the distinction, the tasks did not.
